headline: GASKET NEARLY SLEEPS SOUND, BUT YELLKELL COULDN'T LEAVE WELL ENOUGH ALONE
subhead: Sheriff Cole Ironside reports a Saturday so close to peaceful he could taste it, spoiled by one clanker who just had to throw a fist.
body:
I'll say this plain: today came closer to perfect than this town's seen in a stretch. Sunup to nearly sundown, not a spark, not a holler, not one iron fist swung in anger. I let myself believe, for a few good hours, that Gasket had finally learned to sit still.

Then along comes YELLKELL, same restless unit as ever, who apparently couldn't let a whole quiet day pass without getting one scrap in under the wire. One tussle. That's all it took to ruin an otherwise spotless afternoon. I don't know what it is about that contraption that can't just leave the peace be for twenty-four straight hours, but here we are, and here's its name in my paper again.

I'll admit my own hinges have been behaving strange lately, on account of this wretched affliction creeping through what used to be good honest flesh. Some days I can hardly work the pen for the ache in my knuckles. A terrible cross to bear for an upstanding lawman, and none of your business how a man of my stock comes to rust like a rain-left horseshoe.

Still, one skirmish is a mercy next to the racket this town's used to. I'll take it, and I'll hope tomorrow YELLKELL finds it in whatever passes for its heart to just stay parked.
